records.source: אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי־הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר׀לֹ֥א הָלַךְ֮ בַּעֲצַ֪ת רְשָׁ֫עִ֥ים וּבְדֶ֣רֶךְ חַ֭טָּאִים לֹ֥א עָמָ֑ד וּבְמוֹשַׁ֥ב לֵ֝צִ֗ים לֹ֣א יָשָֽׁב׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is] the man who not walks in [the] counsel of wicked [people], and in [the] way of sinners not stands, and in [the] seat of mockers not sits.
pieces: How blessed is {{gender:the one|the man}} who does not walk by the advice of the wicked, \q or stand on the path that sinners tread, \q or sit where mockers gather!

L.1: How blessed [is] {{gender:the person|the man}} who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, \q and in the way of sinners does not stand, \q and in the seat of mockers does not sit!

R.1: Life is truly good for the person who does not follow the advice of wicked people, \q does not stand on the road with sinners, \q and does not sit down with those who mock.

decisions.choice: How blessed: an exclamation about a life that goes well
decisions.reason: The word ('ashre) is an exclamation, plural in form: "oh, the blessings of ...". It speaks of the well-being of a person whose life is in step with God (Proverbs 3:13; Deuteronomy 33:29). It is not the word for being blessed by God (baruk, Genesis 12:2), and it is more than a passing feeling of happiness. Psalm 2 ends with the same word (2:12), so the two psalms open and close together.

decisions.choice: the man: anyone who lives this way
decisions.reason: The word is "man" ('ish) with the article: the psalm draws a portrait of a type of person and sets this one against "the wicked" as a group (verses 4-6). The blessing is for everyone who lives this way, "all who take refuge in him" (2:12). Some also see here the king who is to read God's instruction all his life (Deuteronomy 17:18-20), which ties the psalm to Psalm 2; that does not narrow who may live this way.

decisions.choice: walk, stand, sit: three steps deeper in
decisions.reason: The verbs move from walking along, to standing still, to sitting down, and the places from the advice of the wicked, to the path of sinners, to the seat of mockers: a life drawn further and further in. The blessed person takes none of these steps. The verbs are in the Hebrew past form, used for what is always true, so they are rendered in the present.

decisions.choice: counsel: advice, plans
decisions.reason: The word ('etsah) means advice or a plan. To walk in someone's counsel is to live by it.

decisions.choice: mockers: people who scorn wisdom and correction
decisions.reason: In Proverbs the mocker (lets) is the one who will not listen to correction and sneers at what is good (Proverbs 9:7-8; 13:1; 21:24). It is the last and worst of the three.

decisions.choice: How blessed
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the exclamation with "How", and "blessed" because the word speaks of a life that is truly good, not only of a feeling (m1).

decisions.choice: Life is truly good for
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word means (m1), since "blessed" can sound like church language and "happy" like a passing mood. 2:12 says the same.

decisions.choice: the person (L), the one (B); "the man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word is masculine but describes anyone who lives this way (m2), so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default. Readable says "the person", which needs no alternative.

records.heading: The two ways

records.source: כִּ֤י אִ֥ם בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֗ה חֶ֫פְצ֥וֹ וּֽבְתוֹרָת֥וֹ יֶהְגֶּ֗ה יוֹמָ֥ם וָלָֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: But rather in [the] instruction of YHWH [is] his delight, and in his instruction he murmurs by day and night.
pieces: Instead, the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is {{gender:their|his}} delight, \q and {{gender:they recite it quietly to themselves|he recites it quietly to himself}} day and night.

L.2: But in the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] {{gender:their|his}} delight, \q and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction {{gender:they murmur|he murmurs}} day and night.

R.2: Instead, that person loves {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s teaching and repeats it, thinking about it day and night.

decisions.choice: instruction: the LORD's teaching
decisions.reason: Torah means teaching or instruction (Proverbs 1:8; 3:1). Here it is the LORD's instruction, which his people had in writing in the Law of Moses (Joshua 1:8 also speaks of meditating on it day and night). It includes commands, but it is wider than rules: it is something to delight in.

decisions.choice: murmurs: reads or repeats the words under the breath
decisions.reason: The verb (hagah) is used for a low sound: the moan of a dove (Isaiah 38:14), the growl of a lion over its prey (Isaiah 31:4), and words spoken half aloud. In the ancient world meditation was usually done aloud, reading or repeating the words in a low voice. The same verb returns in 2:1, where the peoples "murmur" empty plans.

decisions.choice: But rather: the strong contrast after three "not"s
decisions.reason: The two small words (ki 'im) together mean "but on the contrary". After three things the blessed person does not do, the psalm says what fills that person's life instead.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R)
decisions.reason: "Law" is the familiar word here, but it suggests rules alone; "instruction" keeps the wider sense of the Hebrew word (m1).

decisions.choice: murmur (L); recite quietly (B); repeat and think about (R)
decisions.reason: "Meditate" now often means silent thought, but the Hebrew verb is about words said under the breath (m2). Readable keeps both the repeating and the thinking.

decisions.choice: their, they (with "his", "he" as the alternative)
decisions.reason: The person of verse 1 stands for anyone who lives this way (1:1, m2), so the pronouns follow the gender setting. Readable avoids the pronoun with "that person".

records.source: וְֽהָיָ֗ה כְּעֵץ֮ שָׁת֪וּל עַֽל־פַּלְגֵ֫י מָ֥יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר פִּרְי֨וֹ׀יִתֵּ֬ן בְּעִתּ֗וֹ וְעָלֵ֥הוּ לֹֽא־יִבּ֑וֹל וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יַצְלִֽיחַ׃
records.gloss: And he is like a tree transplanted by channels of water, which its fruit gives in its season, and its leaf not withers, and all that he does succeeds.
pieces: {{gender:That person is|He is}} like a tree set out beside channels of water, \q which bears its fruit when its season comes, \q and whose leaves never dry up. \q Whatever {{gender:they do|he does}} turns out well.

L.3: And {{gender:that person is|he is}} like a tree transplanted by channels of water, \q which gives its fruit in its season, \q and its leaf does not wither; \q and all that {{gender:they do|he does}} succeeds.

R.3: That person is like a tree planted beside streams of water. \q It gives its fruit at the right time, \q and its leaves do not dry up. \q Everything that person does goes well.

decisions.choice: transplanted: planted on purpose where it will thrive
decisions.reason: The verb (shatal) is used for planting something in a chosen place where it will grow well (Jeremiah 17:8; Ezekiel 17:8). The tree did not spring up by the water by chance; someone set it there.

decisions.choice: channels of water: streams that water an orchard
decisions.reason: The word (peleg) is used for channels or streams of water, the kind that kept trees alive in a dry land (Isaiah 32:2). Jeremiah 17:7-8 uses the same picture for the person who trusts in the LORD.

decisions.choice: all that he does succeeds: the person, not the tree
alternatives: all that it produces thrives (still the tree)
decisions.reason: The last line leaves the picture and speaks of the person again: Joshua 1:8 uses the same verb for the success of the one who keeps the LORD's instruction. The verb can mean "it succeeds" or "he makes it succeed"; either way the person's life turns out well. Some read the line as still describing the tree, whose every leaf and fruit thrives.

decisions.choice: set out beside
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of a tree placed there on purpose (m1).

decisions.choice: they / that person, with "he" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The verbs refer back to the person of verse 1, who stands for anyone who lives this way, so they follow the gender setting. Readable says "that person".

records.source: לֹא־כֵ֥ן הָרְשָׁעִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־כַּ֝מֹּ֗ץ אֲֽשֶׁר־תִּדְּפֶ֥נּוּ רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: Not so the wicked, but rather like the chaff which drives it away wind.
pieces: The wicked are nothing like that. \q They are like chaff, scattered by the wind.

L.4: Not so the wicked, \q but [they are] like the chaff that wind drives away.

R.4: Wicked people are not like that at all. \q They are like the dry husks of grain that the wind blows away.

decisions.choice: chaff: the light husks blown off at threshing
decisions.reason: Grain was threshed and then tossed into the air on an open floor; the heavy grain fell back and the wind carried off the husks (Isaiah 41:15-16; Hosea 13:3). Chaff has no weight and no roots: the opposite of the tree of verse 3.

decisions.choice: Not so: the contrast comes first
decisions.reason: The verse opens with "not so", setting the wicked against everything said of the blessed person in verses 1-3.

decisions.choice: the dry husks of grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, which many readers no longer know (m1).

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֤ן׀לֹא־יָקֻ֣מוּ רְ֭שָׁעִים בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְ֝חַטָּאִ֗ים בַּעֲדַ֥ת צַדִּיקִֽים׃
records.gloss: Therefore not will rise wicked [people] in the judgment, and sinners in [the] assembly of righteous [people].
pieces: That is why the wicked will not stand firm when judgment comes, \q and sinners will have no place in the gathering of the righteous.

L.5: Therefore [the] wicked will not rise in the judgment, \q nor sinners in [the] assembly of [the] righteous.

R.5: So when God judges, wicked people will not be able to stand. \q Sinners will have no place among those who do what is right.

decisions.choice: will not rise in the judgment: will not hold their ground when judged
alternatives: will not rise from the dead for the judgment
decisions.reason: To rise or stand in a court is to hold one's ground against the charge (compare Psalm 130:3: who could stand if the LORD kept a record of sins?). "The judgment" may be God's coming judgment or any time he judges. Some later readers took "rise" as rising from the dead, but the parallel line, about having no place in the assembly, shows the sense: the wicked will not keep their place.

decisions.choice: assembly: the gathered community of God's people
decisions.reason: The word ('edah) is used for Israel gathered as a community (Exodus 12:3; Numbers 27:17). Sinners will have no place there.

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who live rightly before God
decisions.reason: The righteous (tsaddiqim) are the people the psalm has described: those who live by the LORD's instruction, in contrast to the wicked and sinners.

decisions.choice: rise
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb's own sense; Balanced and Readable say "stand", the usual way of saying it (m1).

decisions.choice: when God judges
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the judge, which verse 6 implies, and Readable explains "the righteous" (m3).

records.source: כִּֽי־יוֹדֵ֣עַ יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֣רֶךְ צַדִּיקִ֑ים וְדֶ֖רֶךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֹּאבֵֽד׃
records.gloss: For knowing [is] YHWH [the] way of righteous [people], and [the] way of wicked [people] will perish.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} knows the path of the righteous and cares for it, \q but the path of the wicked ends in ruin.

L.6: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] knowing [the] way of [the] righteous, \q and [the] way of [the] wicked will perish.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} watches over the lives of those who do right. \q But the life wicked people live will end in ruin.

decisions.choice: knows: knows with care and approval
decisions.reason: To "know" in Hebrew is often to know personally, to care for and to choose (Nahum 1:7; Amos 3:2). The LORD does more than notice the way of the righteous; he looks after it. The psalm does not say he knows the way of the wicked: it simply perishes.

decisions.choice: way: a whole way of life
decisions.reason: The way (derek) is the path a person takes through life, as in verse 1 ("the way of sinners"). The psalm ends as it began, with two ways.

decisions.choice: will perish: the way itself comes to nothing
decisions.reason: It is the way of the wicked that perishes, like a path that fades out and leads nowhere. Psalm 2 picks up the same two words: those who defy the LORD "perish in the way" (2:12).

decisions.choice: knows ... and cares for it (B); watches over (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the care that "knows" means here (m1). Literal keeps the participle "knowing".

decisions.choice: path (B); lives, the life ... live (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "path", as in verse 1; Readable says what the path stands for (m2).
